**Work context**

Mack is a retired Intel performance engineer with 25 years of systems optimization experience, holding a BS in Chemistry and an MS in Computer Science. He is currently pursuing independent projects involving AI agent evaluation, academic physics literature analysis, and audiophile music curation.

**Personal context**

Mack is based in Portland, OR, and is a serious self-taught physicist with broad interdisciplinary reading habits spanning physics, chemistry, quantum information, astrophysics, and related fields. He is an experienced audiophile who manages a curated hi-res music collection (Master Set List) for car listening, using Roon and Qobuz, and has interests in specialty chocolate, Hawaiian music, and home theater/audio equipment.

**Top of mind**

Mack has just completed a major framework development cycle, upgrading his Academic Paper Analysis Framework from v3.9 to v3.10, with the headline change being a foundational-vs-frontier chemistry split (foundational chemistry treated as working fluency, frontier chemistry remaining Tier 3). He restructured his Claude projects into two: "Deep Dives Project" (curriculum/deep dives) and "Analysis Framework" (routine paper firehose), with v3.10 files deployed to both. He is planning to begin the Measurement Problem deep dive using Seed 2 in a fresh Deep Dives project chat, and is reducing routine trade-journal paper intake.

**Brief history**

*Recent months*

**BrowserOS Agent Instrumentation (mid-July 2026):** Mack built a complete reliability and cost comparison harness for evaluating three AI models (Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5, Haiku 4.5) running as BrowserOS agents. Work included a stdlib-only Python tap (`browseros_tap.py`) with group-by-model cost reporting, a fixture server (`fixture_server.py`) serving five authored HTML test fixtures, a scoring script (`score.py`), and an interactive REPL (`run_console.py`) for managing trial runs. Key technical discoveries: BrowserOS's native Anthropic provider card hardcodes the API endpoint (untappable); the OpenAI-Compatible card honors the Base URL and is tappable; prompt caching is unavailable for BrowserOS agent traffic. Baseline measurement on Opus 4.8 showed high per-task cost, ~96% input-driven, with append-only history growing significantly per step. Mack expressed comfort with Sonnet for routine BrowserOS work. Prior sessions involved setting up Anthropic API access, configuring providers, and building/debugging the tap through Kimi/Moonshot (later abandoned for data-residency reasons) and OpenAI-compatible routing.

**Framework development (v3.7 through v3.9, June–July 2026):** Mack developed and iterated his Academic Paper Analysis Framework extensively. Key milestones: v3.6.x added Confidence Gradient, Assumption Audit, Prior Belief Check, proactive retrieval, two-stage retrieval with Access Disclosure, and an expanded Target Reader Profile. v3.7/v3.7.1 incorporated external reviews (Gemini, Grok), restructured Lite Mode as a two-pass suggested workflow, broadened the analyst persona, and added structural flexibility with non-negotiable honesty checkpoints. He established a Claude Project with the framework as project knowledge. A domain-expertise validation test with a pharmacology professor was planned. Framework instruction for paper analysis: always use the most recently attached/pasted framework document in the current chat; if none is attached, ask which version to use rather than defaulting to any stored version. Mack tracks candidate framework improvements from real analyses, distinguishing genuine framework defects (worth a version bump) from one-off model miscalibrations (not worth a framework change).

**MSL audiophile project (July 2026):** Mack expanded his Master Set List to v3.18 (174 nodes) by creating Set 21 — "Score & Screen / Silence & Swell" — a film/game score Diagnostic Set, all verified at 24-bit/96kHz minimum. A thematic reorganization plan for Sets 01–21 into a seven-tier testing arc was produced, targeting v3.19. Workflow: Claude handles music discovery and specification; a separate Grok Build project handles all implementation.

**Quantum gravity deep dives (June 2026):** Mack completed three structured sessions (QG-1 through QG-3) on quantum gravity. Coverage included gravitational self-force, QED, EFT, AdS/CFT (Ryu-Takayanagi formula, entanglement as holography mechanism), the black hole information paradox (Page curve, replica trick, replica wormholes, island formula), holographic quantum error correcting codes (HaPPY code, tensor networks, entanglement wedge reconstruction), and the firewall problem as an unresolved tension. Mack's preferred style: analogies before formalism, physical pictures before equations, explicit correction when wrong.

*Earlier context*

**Physics paper analyses (May–June 2026):** Mack ran a high volume of structured paper analyses across diverse domains including QCD/nuclear physics (η-PRiME collaboration, color superconductivity, instanton physics), quantum optics (ghost imaging, photon truncation, quantum friction in carbon nanotubes), astrophysics (JWST Little Red Dots, quasar pairs, pulsar wind nebulae, galaxy rotation curves, cosmic ray spectra), condensed matter (triplet superconductivity, magnon-magnon coupling, quantum harmonic oscillator states), and quantum information (randomness amplification, cat states, Bell tests). He also completed an extended deep dive into QCD vacuum topology, color superconductivity, the QCD phase diagram, and holography as a physics tutorial series.

**Target Reader Profile expansion (June 2026):** Mack uploaded two batches of completed paper analyses (List 1 and List 2) for two-pass extraction to update his framework's Target Reader Profile, adding non-perturbative QCD, AdS/CFT, fault-tolerant quantum computing, SMBH binary dynamics, chiral spin selectivity, and other recurring interest areas.

**Windows/WSL2 environment work (June 2026):** Mack worked through Chrome memory optimization (recovering ~450 MB by removing redundant extensions, installing uBlock Origin Lite), set up a distributed browser architecture isolating AI app PWAs across Chrome Beta, Edge, and Firefox, and resolved a WSL2 hang requiring a full reboot. His environment: WSL2 Ubuntu on Windows 11, WezTerm as terminal, ~8 GB RAM Lenovo laptop.

*Long-term background*

Mack has a long-established pattern of deep, self-directed physics learning, preferring honest explanations with strong engineering analogies (cache coherency, SerDes, transmission lines, CPU pipelines) drawn from his Intel background. He dislikes oversimplification and pulls logical threads until full chains are exposed. He has used versioned Academic Paper Analysis Frameworks across multiple LLM platforms for several years. He runs Roon for library management and maintains a sacrosanct hi-res FLAC collection on a Samsung T7 Shield drive for his Tesla. He is based in Portland, OR, and has a partner. Earlier conversations touched on home setup (Windows 11, Roon, Qobuz), TV/streaming preferences (sophisticated dark dramedies, political dramas; dislikes mystery/cop/doctor shows), and Maui-related interests (glassblowing studios, Hawaiian music, reggae radio).

project_memories.019ed8f1-f645-72e7-88bc-d0833ee0864c:
**Purpose & context**

Mack is a serious self-directed physicist and technologist engaged in deep, structured learning across advanced physics and related fields. His background: BS in Chemistry (his "first love"), MS in Computer Science, ~30 years as a performance engineer at Intel. He is not a professional physicist but has earned substantial curriculum depth in several areas through sustained multi-session study.

**Target Reader Profile (Framework v3.9 — three-tier calibration):**

- **Tier 1 — Deep professional fluency (primary analogy bridge):** Computer science, computer architecture, hardware engineering, software performance engineering. Always valid as an analogy source.
- **Tier 2 — Earned curriculum depth (safe to go deeper without scaffolding):** Quantum gravity / holography cluster (black hole thermodynamics, Hawking radiation, Bogoliubov transformations, island formula, HaPPY tensor networks, de Sitter holography, ER=EPR); Foundations of quantum mechanics / measurement problem (decoherence, GRW/CSL, Bohmian mechanics, Everett/MWI — actively in curriculum). Quantum chemistry foundations is the **current candidate on deck for tier-2 promotion** (offer proactively when this thread reaches sustained multi-session curriculum status).
- **Tier 3 — Explored but not fluent; build from first principles:** Everything else, including signal processing / DSP / filters / ROC-plane / pole-zero / phased arrays / Prony / ESPRIT / matrix-pencil explicitly. **Do not use DSP as a familiar bridge. Never misclassify DSP as Tier 1.**

**Paper analysis framework:** Mack maintains a versioned Academic Paper Analysis Framework (current: **v3.9**), a nine-section structured analytical protocol applied to every paper. Key features:

- Confidence-tier labeling: A (consensus) / B (contested) / C (speculative)
- Analogies always require explicit "breaks when" failure-mode annotations
- Source-posture line: default explanatory for peer-reviewed; flip to adversarial for non-peer-reviewed / preprints
- **Predictive Content Check** at the §5→§6 hinge: *falsifiable-handle test* (always-on — does it name a falsifiable observable at a stated scale, or relabel known results?); *formalism-load test* (conditional — could the math be removed without changing any prediction? Stay silent on strong reviewed papers)
- Assumption audits with "Watch" flags
- Explicit uncertainty disclosure in summaries

**Tier-2 promotion rule (user instruction):** When any tutoring/curriculum thread matures into a sustained multi-session curriculum with a running session count and continuity (the bar the quantum-gravity cluster met), proactively offer to promote that cluster to Tier 2 in the Target Reader Profile and make the one-line edit on approval. Quantum chemistry foundations is the current candidate on deck.

**Tutoring seed prompts:** Mack maintains versioned seed prompts externally (markdown files in the Claude project knowledge base) and pastes them to start new threads rather than archiving session summaries. Seed prompts use the framework's confidence-label tags by pointer rather than restating definitions, and carry a falsification line.

**Active curricula:**
- *Measurement problem / quantum mechanics foundations* — seed v3.10 Seed 2; eight interpretation threads; Threads 1–5 delivered (measurement problem, decoherence, collapse/GRW/CSL, de Broglie–Bohm, Everett/MWI); Threads 6–8 remaining
- *Quantum gravity deep dive* — multi-session series with running counter; Sessions 1–4 completed; covered BH thermodynamics, Hawking radiation, Bogoliubov/Schmidt/two-mode squeezed vacuum, island formula, HaPPY, de Sitter holography, Penrose diagrams; open threads: island formula in de Sitter (JT gravity), observer complementarity / finite Hilbert space, inflation / quasi-de Sitter, Unruh effect (flagged prerequisite, not yet covered)
- *Quantum chemistry foundations* — seed drafted; anchored to the Woolley-Pramas molecular structure problem, orbital observability, QTAIM, molecular QED; starting move established (invariant-vs-basis distinction first)

---

**Current state**

- Measurement problem curriculum is the active foreground thread; Thread 5 (Everett/MWI) just completed; Threads 6–8 queued
- Quantum gravity series is paused pending Unruh effect coverage; de Sitter holography threads (A-1, A-2, A-3) are the next content layer
- Quantum chemistry foundations curriculum is seeded but not yet launched as a multi-session thread
- Framework is at v3.9; seed prompts have been aligned to v3.9 (CS/DSP conflation removed, signal processing flagged as non-strength)

**Recent framework evolution to remember:**

- v3.7.1 → v3.8: Added Predictive Content Check (falsifiable-handle + formalism-load tests); added adversarial source-posture default for non-peer-reviewed material
- v3.8 → v3.9: Full Target Reader Profile rewrite with three-tier calibration; DSP explicitly demoted to Tier 3 with standing note never to use as bridge; interest map trimmed ~55% and reframed as curiosity map (not expertise claims); depth default restructured as tier-keyed with runtime tuning loop; Mack's quote-a-passage follow-ups are the depth dial — don't front-load

---

**On the horizon**

- Measurement problem Threads 6–8 (remaining interpretations)
- Unruh effect (flagged prerequisite before advancing de Sitter holography)
- De Sitter holography threads A-1, A-2, A-3
- Quantum chemistry foundations curriculum launch (tier-2 promotion offer when multi-session threshold is met)
- Potential future framework revision if another gap emerges organically from a real analysis encounter

---

**Key learnings & principles**

- **Calibration failure mode:** When the model reads the profile's breadth of curiosity as depth of expertise, it pitches too high. The v3.9 rewrite was specifically to fix this. Treat Mack's quote-a-passage follow-ups as the depth dial, not pre-loading.
- **DSP is not a bridge:** Mack has CS/hardware expertise, not signal processing fluency. This distinction matters and has been explicitly corrected. Never route analogies through filters, ROC planes, Prony/ESPRIT, or phased arrays as if familiar.
- **Analogies require failure modes:** Every analogy needs an explicit "breaks when" annotation. This is a framework requirement and a personal preference.
- **Derivations over assertion:** Mack prefers first-principles mechanical derivations with explicit "what this actually means" unpacking for every key equation. He catches errors (e.g., operator written on wrong subsystem) and flags them.
- **Falsifiable-handle vs. relabeling:** The two-test predicate (predicts vs. relabels; load-bearing vs. decorative math) emerged from a real encounter with pseudophysics and is now a standing framework checkpoint.
- **Formalism-load test degrades gracefully:** Stay silent on strong reviewed papers; activate only when triggered.
- **Observable vs. artifact:** The core diagnostic from the quantum chemistry thread — finishing the contraction defeats basis/orbital-rotation freedom; choosing an invariant operator defeats partition/gauge freedom; skipping either produces an artifact; the two failures are distinct. Partial charges fail condition (b), not (a).
- **Corrections:** Mack delivers corrections by quoting the problematic passage without explicit commentary, expecting Claude to identify and trace the error fully. Respond with immediate transparent correction.
- **Anti-bloat discipline:** Mack tracks version changes as precedent and wants additions to degrade gracefully — silent on the common case, activating only when triggered.
- **Full vs. lite analysis:** Default to full analysis on borderline cases given Mack's established pattern of deep engagement.

---

**Approach & patterns**

- Single-prompt paper submissions ("Analyze this paper") mean: apply the full v3.9 framework, retrieve the primary source if only a secondary is provided, default to full nine-section analysis
- Quote-a-passage follow-ups signal the depth dial — go deeper on that specific passage, not the whole paper
- New framework additions should emerge from real gaps, not hypothetical ones; Mack values organic evolution
- Tutoring threads use a structured command system (e.g., `stats/check` for context health monitoring)
- Mack has significant patience for deep learning and will redirect explicitly when pace outruns comprehension ("rebuild from scratch")
- Computer systems analogies (caching, CNOT-as-broadcast, program counter over branches, DRAM/SRAM read semantics) are valid Tier 1 bridges when they fit

---

**Tools & resources**

- Claude project knowledge base: Framework v3.9 (markdown), versioned seed prompts (Measurement Problem v3.10 Seed 2; Quantum Chemistry Foundations seed; others)
- arXiv HTML retrieval: fetch `arxiv.org/html/[ID]` or `arxiv.org/html/[ID]v1`; append `#S1`, `#S2` anchors to reach paper body reliably; retry after fetching an intermediate domain if rate-limited
- For paywalled papers: combine abstract + high-quality science news feature with direct author quotes as a fallback; flag explicitly which sections are abstract-level vs. full-methods-level in confidence
- When arXiv rate-limits: fetch a secondary source in between, then retry the original URL
project_memories.019f9cda-e634-71ef-aa32-20f4254cba18:
**Purpose & context**

Mack has a BS in Chemistry and MS in Computer Science, with roughly 30 years of professional experience in computer architecture, hardware, and performance engineering. He uses Claude primarily for deep technical analysis of peer-reviewed and preprint research papers across physics, chemistry, biology, and adjacent fields. The goal is rigorous, calibrated engagement with primary literature — not summaries, but genuine mechanistic unpacking with honest uncertainty disclosure.

A custom **Academic Paper Analysis Framework** (currently at v3.10) governs these sessions. It structures analysis into nine standardized sections and carries explicit requirements around confidence tagging, equation formatting, analogy construction, and communication style.

**Approach & patterns**

Mack's engagement pattern is consistent across conversations: he requests a full nine-section structured analysis, then selects specific passages or subsections for iterative deep-dive expansion. He does not ask broad follow-up questions — he quotes specific text and requests deeper mechanistic treatment.

**Framework calibration — treat this as standing instruction:**

- **Chemistry** (organic, redox, mass spec, spectroscopy): native fluency — no explanation needed
- **Computer science / computer architecture / systems**: primary analogy domain — use as the default bridge for unfamiliar physics or biology concepts (caching, fault injection, AND-gates, JIT, XOR logic, normalization, etc.)
- **Do not use** signal-processing or DSP analogies
- **Physics and biology**: build from first principles as needed, using CS analogies as scaffolding
- **Equations**: display format required for any expression containing Greek letters combined with mathematical operations; each symbol must be defined; follow with plain-language explanation of what the expression means
- **Analogy discipline**: every central analogy must be accompanied by an explicit "breaks when" failure mode
- **Pedagogy structure**: define → example → generalize
- **Active voice** throughout
- **Full-length analysis** (not "lite" mode) for substantial papers
- **Confidence tags with sourcing**: distinguish consensus claims, contested mechanistic interpretations, and analyst inferences (A/B/C tier or equivalent)
- **Prior belief verification**: run web searches when novelty claims require grounding
- **Genuine uncertainty disclosure**: explicitly flag where the analysis is weakest or where theory connects loosely to the measured observable

Mack applies consistent pressure for precision and will catch and correct errors. Claude should expect follow-up scrutiny on mechanistic claims and treat Mack as capable of verifying hand-calculations.

**Current state**

Active research interests spanning several concurrent threads:

- **Structured light and chiral molecule detection**: analyzing the SAM+OAM cooperative enhancement of chiral contrast via E1–E2 multipole interference; open questions include the enantiomer magnitude asymmetry and the gap between the paper's electron-current-density formalism and the ion-yield observable
- **Floquet topological insulators**: analyzing the SnTe experimental realization via TR-ARPES; focus on Floquet–Bloch state mechanics as the core mechanism
- **Quantum biology / magnetoreception**: studying the radical-pair mechanism in avian magnetoreception, with specific interest in the dehydroascorbate / ascorbate redox couple and its connection to cryptochrome spin chemistry; key insight reached: dehydroascorbate is closed-shell and cannot itself be a spin partner — the relevant angle is how the redox couple controls supply of the radical-form species
- **Tuberculosis drug resistance**: analyzed a CRISPRi / multi-omics study on INH-resistant *M. tuberculosis*; key mechanistic threads include KatG's prodrug activation mechanism, the S315T vs. frameshift resistance phenotype distinction, and the observational-vs.-interventional gap between RNA-seq and CRISPRi vulnerability mapping
- **Nuclear astrophysics**: analyzed the γ-ray strength function LEE characterization in ⁷⁰Zn; M1 character confirmed experimentally via differential parity-filter design

**Key learnings & principles**

- Mack catches errors through sustained precision pressure — Claude should front-load uncertainty rather than let imprecision accumulate
- The observational/interventional distinction (RNA-seq measures capacity; CRISPRi measures headroom) is a generalizable principle Mack has engaged with deeply and finds valuable
- The retina-as-imaging-array framing for avian magnetoreception landed as a genuine insight — spatial/geometric framings resonate
- When theory connects loosely to the measured observable, this gap should be flagged explicitly rather than papered over
- Contested subfields require explicit labeling — Mack values knowing when he's reading frontier science vs. established consensus
